## Context / Problem
`examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md` Step 7 (lines 741-785) sweeps for siblings of the
proven root cause along two independent, independently-triggered axes — a construct sweep and a
parity sweep — and already requires each confirmed sibling to be **fixed under the same RED→GREEN
discipline**, with a filed+`discovered_from`-linked ticket as the fallback for one left out of
scope (`SKILL.md:759-762`, `783-785`). What is missing is the *class-level design review*: the
siblings never become declared, reviewable scope on the bug ticket, so the fix for one instance is
never reviewed as a design for the family. In the 7–21 Aug 2026 window families were fixed one
sibling per ticket (`git_adapter` by-path loads ×3, nested-pytest `--basetemp` ×3, repo-isolation
guards ×4, sidecar keying ×3).

The plan-review hook this needs already exists on both ends:
- `SKILL.md:562-568` (Phase 1 exit gate) already tells the agent to declare `file_impact` and run
  `rebar review-plan <id>` before Phase 2 for any fix whose blast radius reaches non-test code.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py:191` (`bug_blast_radius_escalates`), consumed at
  `orchestrator.py:245` and `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py:127`, escalates such a bug
  out of the light advisory tier into the full, blocking-capable rubric.

Step 7 does not reference either. Story `emulsible-beneficent-caiman` (`1dd5-1880-17d0-4ac0`, open)
adds a separate repeat-fix escalation; this story adds the agent-side directive that turns a
confirmed sibling set into declared scope and routes it through the review that already escalates.
Approved 2026-08-21.

## Approach
Amend `examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md` Step 7 (741-785) with a **class-review step**
that fires only when the Axis-1 construct sweep confirms ≥1 semantic sibling:

1. Every confirmed sibling becomes its own `## Acceptance Criteria` checkbox on the bug ticket
   (path + symbol), plus one criterion that a construct-uniqueness guard (or equivalent structural
   check) passes over the class.
2. Before Phase 2 continues past the first sibling, record every sibling path via
   `rebar set-file-impact` and run `rebar review-plan <bug>` — cross-referencing, not restating,
   the Phase-1 exit-gate directive at `SKILL.md:562-568`. Recording the sibling paths is what makes
   `bug_blast_radius_escalates` fire, so the class-level plan is scored by the full rubric rather
   than the light bug tier.
3. A `BLOCK` verdict stops Phase 2 until the plan is revised and re-reviewed. (`review-plan --force`
   is NOT a bypass for this — per `rebar review-plan --help` it only re-runs a review over a current
   attestation; it cannot override a `BLOCK`. The stop is agent discipline, because a bug is not
   claim-gated.)
4. Keep the step portable: gate the rebar command names on "when the project's tracker is rebar,"
   and state the generic equivalent (declare the sibling set as the change's scope and put the
   class-level plan through the project's plan review) for every other tracker.

Do NOT restate the Phase-1 directive; Step 7 links to it.

Separately, `docs/plan-review-gate.md` currently documents the bug tier as never-blocking
(`486-489`: "a bug can be coached but never BLOCKED"; `1348-1353`: "never blocks a bug — precheck
downgrades every DET finding to advisory (`det_blocking:[]`) … `route_criteria` returns only
`BUG_TIER_CRITERIA` for a `bug`"), which the shipped blast-radius escalation contradicts. Add the
escalation as a named subsection under `## R4 — the necessity probe + the lightweight bug review
tier` (line 1325) and correct the two contradicting passages so the "if the review blocks" premise
above is documented rather than denied.

There is NO `examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/phases/` directory and NO dossier template artifact —
the dossier is prose at `SKILL.md:182-232`. No dossier-template edit is in scope.

## Scope
- `examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md` — Step 7 only (741-785).
- `docs/plan-review-gate.md` — new subsection under `## R4` (1325), plus corrections at 486-489
  and 1348-1353.

Not in scope and deliberately untouched: `examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/test-design.md` (pinned
byte-identical to `examples/agent-skills/shared/test-design.md` by
`tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py:29`); the skill frontmatter block (linted by
`scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py`, which globs `**/SKILL.md` frontmatter only and does not read
Step 7).

## Testing
Documentation change; no production code path changes. Gates that read the touched files:
`python scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py` (frontmatter unchanged),
`pytest tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py` (shared copy untouched),
`python scripts/check_docs_index.py`, and `make lint`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Step 7 carries the class-review step: `awk '/^## Step 7 — Sweep for siblings/,/^## Reporting back/' examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md | grep -c "review-plan"` returns ≥ 1 (returns `0` today).
- [ ] Step 7 requires the sibling set to be recorded as file impact before the review: `awk '/^## Step 7 — Sweep for siblings/,/^## Reporting back/' examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md | grep -q "set-file-impact"` exits 0.
- [ ] Step 7 requires every confirmed sibling to become its own acceptance-criterion checkbox: `awk '/^## Step 7 — Sweep for siblings/,/^## Reporting back/' examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md | grep -qi "acceptance criteri"` exits 0.
- [ ] Step 7 cross-references the Phase-1 exit-gate directive instead of restating it: `awk '/^## Step 7 — Sweep for siblings/,/^## Reporting back/' examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md | grep -qi "phase 1"` exits 0, and the Step-7 range contains no second copy of the `bug_blast_radius_escalates` explanation — `awk '/^## Step 7 — Sweep for siblings/,/^## Reporting back/' examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md | grep -c "blast radius"` returns ≤ 1.
- [ ] Step 7 stays portable — the rebar command names are conditioned on the tracker and a generic equivalent is stated: `awk '/^## Step 7 — Sweep for siblings/,/^## Reporting back/' examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md | grep -qi "tracker"` exits 0.
- [ ] `docs/plan-review-gate.md` documents the blast-radius escalation under R4: `awk '/^## R4 — the necessity probe/,/^## The CI rigor signal/' docs/plan-review-gate.md | grep -q "bug_blast_radius_escalates"` exits 0 (returns nothing today).
- [ ] The two contradicting never-blocks passages are corrected: `grep -n "coached but never BLOCKED" docs/plan-review-gate.md` and `grep -n "never blocks a bug" docs/plan-review-gate.md` each either return nothing or return a line that also names the escalation exception.
- [ ] No collateral edits: `git diff --name-only origin/main` lists only `examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md` and `docs/plan-review-gate.md`.
- [ ] Gates pass: `python scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py`, `pytest tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py -q`, `python scripts/check_docs_index.py`, and `make lint` all exit 0.

## Review remediation (2026-08-21)
- Removed `examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/phases/` from Scope and dropped the "dossier template" deliverable: that directory does not exist (the skill ships exactly `SKILL.md`, `test-design.md`, `llm-behavioral-taxonomy.md`) and there is no dossier template — the dossier is prose at `SKILL.md:182-232`.
- Corrected the inverted premise: Step 7 does not "only say to file or link a ticket for each hit" — `SKILL.md:759-762` already mandates "Fix each confirmed sibling under the same RED→GREEN discipline", with ticket-filing as the out-of-scope fallback (same shape at `783-785` for Axis 2).
- Corrected "requires a construct sweep and a parity sweep": `SKILL.md:743-745` states the two axes are independent with independent triggers — enter on *either*, and skip entirely for a one-off single-surface bug.
- Narrowed the claimed new content: `rebar review-plan <id>` before Phase 2, with `file_impact` declared, already exists at `SKILL.md:562-568`. The genuinely new content is siblings-as-AC-checkboxes plus a Step-7 cross-reference to that directive; Step 7 must link rather than duplicate.
- Replaced AC#1: `grep -n "review-plan" examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md` passes today (exit 0, line 564) with zero implementation, and "landing inside Step 7" was prose, not part of the command. Every criterion is now an `awk`-range command scoped to Step 7 that fails on the current tree.
- Removed the `--force` claim: `rebar review-plan --help` defines `--force` as "re-run the review even if a current attestation exists" (and bypassing the not-yet-claimable fast-fail). It does not override a `BLOCK`, so there was nothing to abstain from.
- Relocated and widened the docs edit: `docs/plan-review-gate.md` has no "bug escalation" section, and it actively contradicts the shipped escalation at `:486-489` ("a bug can be coached but never BLOCKED") and `:1348-1353` ("never blocks a bug … `det_blocking:[]` … `route_criteria` returns only `BUG_TIER_CRITERIA`"). A one-sentence addition would have left three contradicting passages standing, so the escalation now lands as a subsection under `## R4` (line 1325) with both passages corrected.
- Added the portability conditioning for Step 7 (`project.portability` is blocking and active per `.rebar/criteria_routing.json`); Step 7 is currently tracker-generic, so bare `rebar` command names would make it rebar-only.
- Named the real consumers in Scope: `scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py` lints `**/SKILL.md` frontmatter only and cannot check Step 7; `tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py:29` pins `test-design.md` byte-identical to the shared copy.
